classification.difficultyReason: Maintain a fixed compass radius through a dependent sequence of intersecting circles, then construct an enclosing circle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Set your compasses to a radius of 3 cm, and do not change the radius again until the final part of this question.

answer.worked: Set the distance between the compass point and pencil tip to 3 cm using a ruler. Keep this setting for parts b–i.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Choose a point $O$ in the middle of your page and draw a circle with centre $O$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $O$ and radius 3 cm.
answer.worked: Place the compass point at $O$ and draw the first circle with radius 3 cm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Choose any point $A$ on the circle, and draw a second circle with centre $A$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $A$ and radius 3 cm, passing through $O$.
answer.worked: Mark $A$ on the first circle. Without changing the compass setting, draw the second circle with centre $A$. Since $OA=3\text{ cm}$, this circle passes through $O$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Let the two circles intersect at $B$ and $F$.

answer.short: The two intersections are labelled $B$ and $F$.
answer.worked: Label the two intersections of the circles with centres $O$ and $A$ as $B$ and $F$. Either orientation of these labels is valid.

children.label: e
children.prompt: With centre $B$, draw a third circle, cutting the first circle at $A$ and $C$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $B$ and radius 3 cm; its other intersection with the first circle is $C$.
answer.worked: Keep the radius at 3 cm and draw a circle with centre $B$. One intersection with the first circle is $A$; label the other $C$.

children.label: f
children.prompt: With centre $C$, draw a fourth circle, cutting the first circle at $B$ and $D$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $C$ and radius 3 cm, intersecting the first circle at $B$ and $D$.
answer.worked: Draw the radius-3 cm circle with centre $C$. Label its new intersection with the first circle $D$; the other intersection is $B$.

children.label: g
children.prompt: With centre $D$, draw a fifth circle, cutting the first circle at $C$ and $E$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $D$ and radius 3 cm, intersecting the first circle at $C$ and $E$.
answer.worked: Draw the radius-3 cm circle with centre $D$. Its intersections with the first circle are the existing point $C$ and the new point $E$.

children.label: h
children.prompt: With centre $E$, draw a sixth circle; this circle should cut the first circle at $D$ and $F$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $E$ and radius 3 cm, intersecting the first circle at $D$ and $F$.
answer.worked: Draw the radius-3 cm circle with centre $E$. Check that it passes through both $D$ and the previously labelled point $F$.

children.label: i
children.prompt: With centre $F$, draw a seventh circle; this circle should cut the first at $E$ and $A$.

answer.short: Circle with centre $F$ and radius 3 cm, intersecting the first circle at $E$ and $A$.
answer.worked: Draw the radius-3 cm circle with centre $F$. Check that its intersections with the first circle are $E$ and $A$.

children.label: j
children.prompt: Change the setting of the compasses to 6 cm. Now draw a circle with centre $O$ that just touches the outsides of the six outer circles.

answer.short: A circle with centre $O$ and radius 6 cm encloses and touches all six outer circles.
answer.worked: Set the compass radius to 6 cm and draw a circle with centre $O$. Each outer circle has its centre 3 cm from $O$ and has radius 3 cm, so its farthest point from $O$ is $3+3=6\text{ cm}$. The new circle therefore touches the outside of each of the six outer circles.

spec.description: Authored completed construction: seven radius-3 cm circles centred at O and the six successive intersections A–F, enclosed by a radius-6 cm circle centred at O. Rotation and reflection are arbitrary because A is freely chosen.
spec.mathematics: A–F lie successively around the first circle at equal chord distances of 3 cm. Every outer circle has radius 3 cm and its centre is 3 cm from O, giving internal tangency with the radius-6 cm enclosing circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no circles, labels or construction marks are supplied in the student question.
